t: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used to provide assistance to, or to pay the salaries of personnel who carry out a market promotion program pursuant to section 203 of the Agricultural Trade Act of 1978 (7 U.S.C. 5623) that provides assistance to, the U.S. Mink Export Development Council or any mink industry trade association.

fable.w: This is an appropriations limitation barring funds from being used to assist the U.S. Mink Export Development Council or mink industry trade associations. The tempting reading is that naming a "Council" and an industry trade association signals outside-party involvement, but these entities are only identified as barred recipients of assistance. Nothing has the federal government consulting them, or giving them a hearing, comment opportunity, or right to sue, before a federal decision.
fable.s: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used to provide assistance to, or to pay the salaries of personnel who carry out a market promotion program

opus.w: This is an appropriations limit that bars funds from going to certain industry groups. The outside parties it names are only potential recipients of assistance, and applying for or receiving benefits does not count as participation. Nothing here requires the government to consult outsiders, hold a hearing or comment period, or give anyone a right to sue before a federal decision. Mentioning private trade associations is not enough to make this participation.
opus.s: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used to provide assistance to, or to pay the salaries of personnel who carry out a market promotion program pursuant to section 203 of the Agricultural Trade Act of 1978 (7 U.S.C. 5623) that provides assistance to, the U.S. Mink Export Development Council or any mink industry trade association.
opus.b: 1. **Analysis.** The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section names outside parties: the U.S. Mink Export Development Council and mink industry trade associations. That reading fails. These groups appear only as possible recipients of program assistance, and the section bars funding to them. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to sue over a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a spending restriction that prohibits the use of federal funds for specific market promotion programs involving certain industry groups. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory process with outside parties. The mention of the U.S. Mink Export Development Council is solely to identify which programs are ineligible for funding, not to establish a participatory role for that group in federal decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds made available in this Act may be used to provide assistance to, or to pay the salaries of personnel who carry out a market promotion program pursuant to section 203 of the Agricultural Trade Act of 1978 (7 U.S.C. 5623) that provides assistance to, the U.S. Mink Export Development Council or any mink industry trade association.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that restricting funds for a "market promotion program" implies some form of consultation or coordination with the industry group mentioned (U.S. Mink Export Development Council). However, the text is a negative restriction on spending ("None of the funds... may be used"), not a mandate for interaction. It does not require the government to consult, coordinate, or hold hearings with the council or any outside party; it simply prohibits funding them. There is no mechanism for outside participation described.
